title: Filtering Above-Average Values with Scalar Subqueries
realWorldScenario: Merchandising analysts want to identify high-value products priced above the overall average catalog price.
questionStatement: Write a query on `products` to find all products whose `price` is strictly greater than the average price of all active products (`is_active = true`). Return `id`, `name`, `category`, and `price`, ordered by `price` descending.
starterCode:
-- Products priced above active average
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  category,
  price
FROM products
WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products WHERE is_active = true)
ORDER BY price DESC;
hints: Write a subquery in parentheses that computes AVG(price) for active products.
Compare price > (subquery) in the outer WHERE clause.

testCases.description: Verify products priced above average active price ($170.82)
